The claim states that the solution avoids transferring invisible geometry to the GPU to prevent prohibitive VRAM usage (citing ~4.5 GB for a 256^3 world). The evidence in Source [S1] explicitly calculates that a 256x256x256 world without culling requires ~4.5GB of GPU RAM. It further explains that using an Octree for spatial partitioning allows for visibility determination (identifying which cubes are visible) and frustum culling, thereby reducing the number of cubes sent to the GPU. The comment by Gustavo Maciel confirms the 4.5GB figure for the full world, and the answer by DeadMG confirms that the Octree approach reduces the visible cube count significantly, thus avoiding the transfer of the full invisible geometry.
